promptBuilder.promptBulderPromptingExplainer:
The left input field is for the system prompt, here you should enter how the LLM should behave/act/respond and give it a more or less static task description. The right input field is for the user prompt, which is the variable part the system prompt should be applied to.
Define variables above and reference them in either prompt with the {{variableName}} syntax — right-clicking inside a prompt field opens a menu to insert them. When you run experiments the current variable values are filled in, and when you manifest a best prompt the variables become the documented inputs of the model.
promptBuilder.promptBuilderVariablesDescription: Create variables and use them in the system or user prompt with the {{variableName}} syntax. Their current values are filled in when experiments run, and they become the inputs of a manifested prompt.

promptBuilder.promptBuilderTemperatureInfo:
Temperature is a parameter that controls the randomness or creativity of the model's responses. It adjusts how the model generates text by affecting the probability distribution of the next word or token in the sequence.
Low Temperature (e.g., 0.1 - 0.5): Responses are more deterministic and focused
Medium Temperature (e.g., 0.5 - 1.0): Balances between creativity and predictability
High Temperature (e.g., 1.0 - 2.0): Responses are more diverse and less predictable
promptBuilder.promptBuilderTop_PInfo:
Top-p (also known as nucleus sampling) is a parameter that controls the randomness and creativity of the model's responses by restricting the choice of possible next words or tokens. It influences how the model selects the next word by limiting the probability distribution to a specific subset of words.
Low Top-p (e.g., 0.1 - 0.3): The selection is more restricted and focused. Only the most probable words are considered, leading to more deterministic and focused responses
Medium Top-p (e.g., 0.4 - 0.7): Provides a balanced mix of creativity and predictability. The range of considered words is broader, allowing the model to include both common and less likely words
High Top-p (e.g., 0.8 - 1.0): The selection is broader and less restricted. The model considers a wider range of words, resulting in more creative and less predictable responses
promptBuilder.promptBuilderTop_KInfo: The Top-k parameter changes how the model selects tokens for output. A Top-k of 1 means the selected token is the most probable among all the tokens in the model's vocabulary (also called greedy decoding), while a topK of 3 means that the next token is selected from among the 3 most probable using the temperature. For each token selection step, the topK tokens with the highest probabilities are sampled. Tokens are then further filtered based on Top-p  with the final token selected using temperature sampling.
promptBuilder.promptBuilderMax_LengthInfo: Max_length: This parameter defines the upper boundary for the length of the generated text. Once the model reaches this token limit, it will stop generating further text, even if the completion is not fully finished.

promptBuilder.promptBuilderJudgeCouncilInfo:
A council sends the run's responses to several judge models at once and combines their votes. A panel of diverse models is more reliable than any single judge — it cancels out one model's blind spots and biases, which matters most for subjective quality.

Cost: one model call per judge, so a 3-judge council takes roughly 3× the time and spend of a single judge.

When to use it: when the decision matters or the responses are close. A single judge is cheaper and fine for quick checks.

Why an odd number: an odd panel (3 is a good default) makes a tied vote far less likely. Pick judges from different providers so their mistakes don't correlate; beyond about five, extra judges add cost without adding much independence.
promptBuilder.promptBuilderJudgeChairmanToggleLabel: Break ties with a chairman model
promptBuilder.promptBuilderJudgeChairmanInfo: If the panel ties, a chairman model breaks it by choosing among only the tied responses, given the task and the panel's notes. It runs one extra model call, and only when a tie actually happens. Leave it off to have ties surface as "judges disagreed" for you to decide.
promptBuilder.promptBuilderOptimizeSectionDescription: Improve this prompt automatically with DSPy. Running an optimization saves the prompt, then launches a SAS Job Execution job that rewrites the instructions and picks few-shot examples to maximise the metric, using the runs you marked as Best Response as training data. The result comes back as a new prompt-test for you to review, judge and accept — nothing is applied automatically.

No optimization runs, so a small model that would shine after optimization can still look weak here.

promptBuilder.promptBuilderOptimizeLaunchFailed: Could not launch the optimization job:
promptBuilder.promptBuilderOptimizeLearnMore: When is this useful, and which metric/optimizer should I pick? — user guide
promptBuilder.promptBuilderOptimizeDatasetInfo:
This prompt's experiments: every saved run with a Best Response becomes one training example — quick to start, but only as good as the responses you vouched for.
A governed CAS table: a curated dataset with one column per prompt variable plus a response column — better for larger, team-maintained example sets. The user guide describes the exact schema.
promptBuilder.promptBuilderOptimizeMetricInfo:
Exact match: the answer must reproduce the reference (case and surrounding punctuation ignored) — best for single words or fixed formats.
Token overlap: F1 over the words shared with the reference — partial credit for close answers; a good default for free-form text.
LLM judge: another model decides whether the answer conveys the same meaning — the most flexible and the most expensive (extra calls).
promptBuilder.promptBuilderOptimizeOptimizerInfo:
Bootstrap few-shot: keeps your instruction and picks strong worked examples to teach with — fast and cheap, a good first run.
MIPROv2: additionally proposes and trials rewritten instructions — often stronger, but it makes many more model calls and needs the optuna package in the compute context.
GEPA: evolves the instruction reflectively — the judge model reads why each answer scored poorly (its own reasoning when the metric is the judge) and proposes improved instructions. Usually the strongest on hard tasks and the most model calls; it selects no few-shot examples.
promptBuilder.promptBuilderOptimizeHistorySkippedPerfe: The optimization phase was skipped: the baseline already scored perfectly on the validation split, so the optimizer had no room to improve. Add harder examples or pick a stricter metric, then optimize again.

ragBuilder.ragBuilderNoEmbeddingModels: No embedding models could be listed from the configured project, so the model name has to be typed. Check the "Embedding model project ID" option and that you can read that project.
ragBuilder.ragBuilderDocSectionHint: Model-card fields, saved onto the Model Manager model as attributes so they appear wherever the setup is opened. Every field is optional — a blank one honestly reads as not stated.
ragBuilder.ragBuilderDocModelPurposeInfo: Why this corpus exists and the decision it supports. A reviewer reads this first, to judge whether everything else is proportionate.
ragBuilder.ragBuilderDocExpectedBenefitInfo: What improves because this corpus exists — faster answers, fewer escalations, wider coverage — and how you would know.
ragBuilder.ragBuilderDocOutOfScopeInfo: Uses this collection must NOT be put to, even though it would return something. Naming them is what makes a later misuse a deviation rather than a surprise.
ragBuilder.ragBuilderDocIntendedUseInfo: Which questions this collection should be asked, and by whom. Retrieval will happily answer questions the corpus cannot support — this is where you say which those are.
ragBuilder.ragBuilderDocLimitationsInfo: Known gaps: coverage, freshness, languages, document quality, anything the extractor or the chunker handles badly. Consumers inherit these whether or not they are written down.
ragBuilder.ragBuilderBackendInfo: Where the chunks and their vectors are stored. Both backends carry the same features, but they are not interchangeable once built — moving a collection means re-ingesting it. A database you hold no credentials for is shown disabled rather than hidden, so you can see it exists and ask for access.
ragBuilder.ragBuilderChunkerInfo: How a document is cut into retrievable pieces. Recursive splits on the largest natural boundary that fits the window (sections, then paragraphs, then sentences); paragraph keeps paragraphs whole and is better for short, well-structured documents.
ragBuilder.ragBuilderCollectionInfo: The table this corpus lives in inside the vector database. Two setups pointing at the same collection write into each other, so give each corpus its own — and a version suffix (…_v1) makes it possible to rebuild alongside the live one and cut over. Lowercase letters, digits and underscores, starting with a letter.
ragBuilder.ragBuilderDeleteFailed: Deleting failed - check your Model Manager permissions.
ragBuilder.ragBuilderDeleteProjectEmptyNote: This project holds no setups. Deleting it removes the project from SAS Model Manager.
ragBuilder.ragBuilderDeleteProjectNote: This deletes the project and the {count} setup(s) it holds from SAS Model Manager. Vector-store collections and CAS tables are NOT touched.
ragBuilder.ragBuilderDeleteSetupNote: This deletes the RAG setup and its generated artifacts from SAS Model Manager. The vector-store collection and its CAS tables are NOT touched - the data stays where it is, and the record of what built it is what disappears.
ragBuilder.ragBuilderEmbedDimsInfo: The width of the vector column, taken from the chosen model — it is a property of the model, not a setting, so it is read-only whenever the model publishes one. It stays editable only for a model registered outside the shipped set, where no width is published. Getting it wrong makes the collection unusable and it cannot be widened afterwards.
ragBuilder.ragBuilderEmbedModelInfo: The model that turns each chunk into a vector, listed from the deployment's embedding model project. It cannot be changed later without re-embedding the whole corpus: a collection can only be searched with the model that built it, because vectors from two models are not comparable.
ragBuilder.ragBuilderExtractorInfo: How text is pulled out of each file. Automatic picks per file format and is almost always right; forcing one applies it to EVERY file, so a PDF read as plain text yields nonsense rather than an error. Some formats need optional Python packages — see the administration guide.
ragBuilder.ragBuilderNewProjectModalHint: A RAG project groups related setups in SAS Model Manager. Its description is what a governance reviewer reads first.
ragBuilder.ragBuilderNewSetupModalHint: A setup is one document corpus wired to one vector-store collection. Choose a project first.
ragBuilder.ragBuilderNoEmbeddingProject: No embedding model project is configured, so no embedding model can be chosen and no setup can be saved. Ask your administrator to set the "Embedding model project ID" option.
ragBuilder.ragBuilderOverlapInfo: How much text each chunk repeats from the previous one, so a sentence split across a boundary is still retrievable whole. Must be smaller than the token window — an overlap at or above it would never advance through the document. Larger overlap means more chunks, more embedding cost and more near-duplicate hits.
ragBuilder.ragBuilderProjectCreateFailed: Creating the RAG project failed - check your Model Manager permissions.
ragBuilder.ragBuilderSetupCreateFailed: Creating the RAG setup failed - check your Model Manager permissions.
ragBuilder.ragBuilderSetupCreated: RAG setup created. Author it below and save.
ragBuilder.ragBuilderSetupNeedsProject: Select a RAG project before creating a setup.
ragBuilder.ragBuilderSourcePathInfo: The folder to crawl, walked recursively, with every readable file treated as a candidate document. A path the ingestion cannot see yields a run that finds nothing rather than one that fails loudly, so check it against the location type on the left.
ragBuilder.ragBuilderTablesCaslibInfo: The caslib holding this pipeline's working tables. It has to be one other people and scheduled jobs can reach: a personal caslib is not offered, because a corpus whose ledger only its author can see cannot be rerun by anyone else or by a schedule.
ragBuilder.ragBuilderTablesPrefixInfo: Prefix for the CAS working tables this pipeline creates — the ledger, the element and chunk tables, the run history. Kept to 20 characters so every generated name stays inside the 32-character CAS limit. Two setups sharing a prefix overwrite each other's ledger.
ragBuilder.ragBuilderTokenLimitInfo: The largest chunk, in tokens. Capped by the embedding model chosen above: text beyond a model window is silently dropped rather than rejected, so an oversized chunk would be embedded from its opening only, and retrieval would then match on text the answer never sees. The ingestion applies a further safety margin below this, because token counts are estimates.
ragBuilder.ragBuilderValidateCaslib: Choose a caslib for the pipeline tables.
ragBuilder.ragBuilderValidateEmbedDims: The embedding dimensions must be a positive number.
ragBuilder.ragBuilderValidateEmbedModel: Choose an embedding model. It decides the vector width and cannot be changed later without re-embedding the whole corpus.
ragBuilder.ragBuilderValidateOverlap: The chunk overlap must be smaller than the embedding token window - at or above it, chunking would never move forward through a document.
ragBuilder.ragBuilderValidateOverlapNegative: The chunk overlap cannot be negative.
ragBuilder.ragBuilderValidateTokenLimit: The embedding token window must be at least 16 tokens.
ragBuilder.ragBuilderDocumentsHint: Where the corpus comes from and how text is read out of it. The ingestion walks this folder on every run and compares what it finds against the ledger, so adding or removing files there is how a corpus changes.
ragBuilder.ragBuilderChunkingHint: How each document is cut into the pieces that get embedded and retrieved. A chunk is the unit an answer is built from, so these settings decide how much context a single hit carries — within whatever the embedding model above can accept.
ragBuilder.ragBuilderEmbeddingHint: The model that turns each chunk into a vector, run as a governed SCR container inside your deployment. Both settings here are fixed for the life of the collection: changing either means rebuilding it.
ragBuilder.ragBuilderTablesHint: The CAS tables this pipeline writes as it runs — the ingestion ledger, the element and chunk tables and the run history. They are rebuilt by each run and are what you read to see what a run did.
ragBuilder.ragBuilderDocSaved: Documentation saved to the Model Manager model.
ragBuilder.ragBuilderDocSaveFailed: Saving the documentation failed - check your Model Manager permissions.
ragBuilder.ragBuilderTokenLimitCeiling: This model accepts at most {max} tokens per chunk.
ragBuilder.ragBuilderTokenLimitUnknown: This model publishes no token limit, so the window is not capped here - check the model card.
ragBuilder.ragBuilderValidateTokenCeiling: The embedding token window exceeds what {model} accepts ({max} tokens). Text beyond a model window is dropped silently, so the excess would never reach the vector.
ragBuilder.ragBuilderOverlapHighNote: {percent}% of the window. Usual practice is 10-20%; above that the repeated text is embedded and stored twice at every boundary, and retrieval returns more near-duplicates.
ragBuilder.ragBuilderOverlapTooLargeNote: The overlap must stay below the {window}-token window - at or above it, chunking never moves forward through a document.
ragBuilder.ragBuilderSaveBlocked: This setup cannot be saved yet - {count} things need attention:
ragBuilder.ragBuilderSaveBlocked1: This setup cannot be saved yet:
ragBuilder.ragBuilderSourceKindInfo: Where the corpus lives. The compute server file system is a path on the SAS Compute server (not your workstation) and suits large corpora already staged on disk. SAS Content is the governed folder tree you see in SAS Drive, read over the Files API - convenient, permission-aware, and slower per document.
ragBuilder.ragBuilderRunLogWaiting: The job has started but has not reported a milestone yet. Embedding runs one call per chunk, so a large corpus can take several minutes before the first line appears.
ragBuilder.ragBuilderRunDoneNote: Run finished. The ingestion ledger is below.
ragBuilder.ragBuilderLedgerRunning: An ingestion has been running for {time}. The ledger is written by the final step of the run, so it shows the PREVIOUS state until this run finishes - it will refresh here automatically.
ragBuilder.ragBuilderIncludeCodeLabel: Ingest source-code files as plain text
ragBuilder.ragBuilderIncludeCodeInfo: Off by default. Source files (.py, .sas, .r, .js, .ts, .sql and ~30 more) are skipped, because a documents folder that sits inside a project would otherwise fill the collection with build scripts that answer no business question. Skipped files are always listed in the ledger and the run log with the reason, never dropped silently. Turn this on for a corpus that is ABOUT code: each file is then indexed as plain text, with its file name kept so a hit can be traced back.
ragBuilder.ragBuilderArtifactsHint: Where the RAG Builder writes the executables it generates from this setup. They are regenerated from the setup on every Generate, so this folder is safe to treat as output rather than source.
ragBuilder.ragBuilderArtifactsFolderInfo: The SAS Content folder receiving the generated ingestion job. Missing folders below the first level are created for you. Put it where the people who will schedule and run this pipeline already look - the default sits under the accelerator content root, which is convenient for the author and invisible to everyone else.
ragBuilder.ragBuilderRegisterNeedsSetup: Select or create a RAG setup first.
ragBuilder.ragBuilderTemplateMissing: retrieve_context.py was not found under the content root - run the deploy-rag-content script first.
ragBuilder.ragBuilderRegistered: Retrieval model registered: retrieve_context.py written as the score code of this setup, with its collection, backend and embedding model baked in.
ragBuilder.ragBuilderFlowStepsMissing: These custom steps are not registered under the content root: {steps}. Run the deploy-rag-content script first.
ragBuilder.ragBuilderFlowGenerated: Studio flow generated in {folder}. Open it in SAS Studio to see or edit the pipeline; regenerate here after changing the setup.
ragBuilder.ragBuilderManifestTitle: Save the setup, generate the ingestion job and the Studio flow, register the retrieval model, and record a new model version.
ragBuilder.ragBuilderManifested: Setup manifested: saved, ingestion job and Studio flow generated in {folder}, retrieval model registered, and a new model version recorded.
ragBuilder.ragBuilderVersionFailed: Everything was generated and registered, but recording a new model version failed - check your permissions on the setup model.
ragBuilder.ragBuilderTestHint: Ask the live collection a question and see the chunks it returns. This is how you tell whether the chunk size and embedding model suit the corpus - the chunks below are exactly what a retrieval would hand an LLM.
ragBuilder.ragBuilderTestTitle: Ask this collection a question and see the chunks that come back. It queries the collection through rag_core, not the registered score code, so a broken retrieve_context.py would still pass here. Nothing is left behind: the job definition it runs is unfiled and deleted afterwards.
ragBuilder.ragBuilderTestQuestionPlaceholder: What does the corpus say about…?
ragBuilder.ragBuilderTestQuestionInfo: Asked the way a user would ask it. The question is embedded with the same model the corpus was built with and matched against the collection - so a question phrased unlike the documents is itself a finding.
ragBuilder.ragBuilderTestTopKInfo: How many chunks come back, highest score first. Ask for more than the retrieval model will use when you are judging a corpus: the chunks just below the cut-off say more about the chunking than the ones above it.
ragBuilder.ragBuilderTestQuestionAdjusted: Asking without the ; & % characters - they cannot survive the trip to the job as a parameter.
ragBuilder.ragBuilderTestSourceMissing: Test-Retrieval.sas was not found under the content root - run the deploy-rag-content script first.
ragBuilder.ragBuilderTestTimeout: The probe is still running after five minutes, which is far longer than a retrieval takes - stopping the wait. Check the compute context and the vector store.
ragBuilder.ragBuilderTestFailed: The retrieval test could not be run - check the browser console and your permissions on the compute context.
ragBuilder.ragBuilderTestNoHits: The probe returned no chunks. If the collection has just been ingested, check the ledger first - an empty collection and an unmatched question look the same from here.
ragBuilder.ragBuilderNeedsComputeContext: No ingestion compute context is configured, and SAS Job Execution refuses a job that does not name one. Set it in the Options pane of this report.
ragBuilder.ragBuilderEnrichHint: Call a prompt you built in the Prompt Builder once per chunk, and keep what it returns: one output becomes the chunk's context header, which is embedded together with the chunk, and any others are stored as tags. It costs one LLM call for every chunk, every time the corpus is re-chunked.
ragBuilder.ragBuilderEnrichProjectInfo: The Prompt Builder project holding the prompt to call. Leaving this on "Do not enrich" is the default and costs nothing: chunks are embedded exactly as the chunker produced them.
ragBuilder.ragBuilderEnrichPromptInfo: A prompt that has been MANIFESTED in the Prompt Builder, with the integrated LLM call - the ingestion runs its score code and reads the answer. A prompt manifested for the Call LLM node of SAS Intelligent Decisioning returns the request instead of making it, and is refused by name.
ragBuilder.ragBuilderEnrichWorkersInfo: How many chunks are enriched at once. Higher finishes sooner and pushes harder on the LLM: a hosted API will rate-limit, and a locally served container queues past roughly four calls per replica.
ragBuilder.ragBuilderEnrichMappingLabel: What each prompt input is given:
ragBuilder.ragBuilderEnrichMappingInfo: Every input of the prompt has to be filled from something the pipeline already holds about the chunk. Nothing is guessed for an input whose name is unfamiliar: a silently wrong mapping would produce a whole corpus of confident nonsense. "Whole document" is capped at 20,000 characters, and a longer document reaches the prompt truncated - the run log says how many.
ragBuilder.ragBuilderEnrichHeaderLabel: Output stored as the context header:
ragBuilder.ragBuilderEnrichNoHeader: Do not store a context header
ragBuilder.ragBuilderEnrichHeaderInfo: This output is prepended to the chunk and embedded WITH it - it is what makes a standalone chunk say where it came from. It is also what costs the accuracy claim its money, so it is worth reading a few in the retrieval test before ingesting a whole corpus. Longer than 1,000 characters and it is cut, because a header that fills the token window pushes the chunk itself out of its own vector.
ragBuilder.ragBuilderEnrichTagsInfo: Stored on the chunk as metadata rather than embedded - a department, a date, a sensitivity flag. They travel into the vector store with the chunk and can be filtered on at retrieval. An output the LLM was asked to produce as JSON is only stored when the response actually parsed: a default value that no model generated is dropped rather than kept.
ragBuilder.ragBuilderEnrichNotManifested: This model carries no readable prompt score code, so there is nothing to call. Manifest it in the Prompt Builder first.
ragBuilder.ragBuilderEnrichNotIntegrated: This prompt was manifested for the Call LLM node of SAS Intelligent Decisioning: it returns the request to make rather than the answer, so an ingestion has nothing to store. Re-manifest it with the integrated LLM call.
ragBuilder.ragBuilderEnrichValidateContract: The selected prompt carries no readable score code, so nothing can be called. Manifest it in the Prompt Builder first.
ragBuilder.ragBuilderEnrichValidateIntegrated: This prompt was manifested for the Call LLM node of SAS Intelligent Decisioning: it returns the request to make rather than the answer, so an ingestion has nothing to store. Re-manifest it with the integrated LLM call.
ragBuilder.ragBuilderEnrichValidateMapping: Choose what fills the prompt input(s) {inputs}.
ragBuilder.ragBuilderEnrichValidateOutputs: This prompt does not return {outputs} - it returns {available}.
ragBuilder.ragBuilderEnrichValidateNothing: Nothing would be stored: choose the output that becomes the context header, or at least one output to keep as a tag.
